Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the grace days, the late fee share, the vacancy target, the highest rent increase, the days of notice and the income multiple.

List every unit on Rent roll with the market rent, the rent, the tenant, the lease dates and the deposit. Loss to lease (rent below the market rent), the days to the lease end and the renewal check fill in.
Record each month of rent on Rent payments: the rent due, the amount paid and the date. Days late, the balance and a payment check fill in, and the collection rate appears on the dashboard.
Write every month a tenant did not pay in full on Arrears with the plan and the last contact. Arrears means rent owed and not paid. Open ones turn red and count in the arrears balance.
Keep leases, renewals and rent increases on their pages. A lease ending soon without an offer turns red so the offer goes out in time. Check your own local rules for notice periods.
Log each empty unit on Vacancy log with the date it emptied and the date it was filled. Days vacant and the rent lost fill in, and a target check shows the slow ones.
Track applicants, showings, move-ins and move-outs on their own pages. Screening shows the income against the rent rule; move-outs show the deposit returned and a settlement check.
Use Security deposits, Late fees, Tenant requests, Unit inspections and Market rent to keep the small facts that cause the big disputes. Check your own local rules for deposits and fees.

Use the 14 calculators: rent roll summary, late rent, payment plan, vacancy cost, rent increase, renew or re-let, deposit, screening, prorated rent, lease end dates, break-even rent, turnover, collection rate and a grid.
Read the Rent Roll and Tenants Dashboard and Charts every week: occupancy, collection rate, arrears, leases ending, vacancy days, renewals and applicants.
Figures about tax, deposits and notices are not legal advice: check your own local rules and check with your own adviser before you act on them.

Work orders: every repair, who did it and what it cost
One row for each repair job with the kind, the priority, the vendor and the cost; open or done, days to fix, how long an open job has waited and a speed check fill in by themselves.
Capex plan: big repairs and replacements with a reserve
One row for each big item (capex: big repairs and replacements) with its planned year, life and cost; years left, the shortfall and the monthly saving needed fill in.
Properties: repairs, reserve, insurance and score
The 16 properties with their value; open work orders, repair cost, the repair allowance, the capex shortfall, the premium and the last inspection score fill in.
Rent units: the units behind the repairs
One row for each rental unit with the tenant and the rent; the repair cost of the last 12 months and its share of the rent fill in. Work orders and messages read the tenant phone from here.
Repairs as a share of rent
Vendors: who does the work, with jobs and spend
The trades and contacts you call, with a rating you give; the number of jobs and the spend fill in from work orders, services, emergencies and inspections.
Recurring service: repeating jobs and when they are due
One row for each service that repeats (heating, gutters, pest, roof) with the last date; the next due date, the days left, the cost for a year and a due check fill in.
Property inspections: score, issues and repair estimate
One row for each inspection with the score of 100 and the issues found; a result check, the good-score flag and the manager phone fill in.
Insurance policies: premium, deductible and renewal date
One row for each property policy with the premium, the deductible (the part of a claim you pay yourself) and the cover; the days to renewal and a renewal check fill in.
Insurance claims: what was claimed and what was paid
One row for each claim with the cause, the amount claimed and the amount paid; open or not, the gap and the days open fill in.
Property tax bills: due dates, payments and late payments
One row for each property tax bill with the amount and the due date; open or paid, days to the due date, late payments and a bill check fill in. Check your own local rules for due dates.
Warranties: what is covered and until when
One row for each warranty with the install date and the years covered; the end date, the days left and an expiry check fill in.
Reserve deposits: money set aside for each property
One row for each monthly deposit into the capex reserve of a property with the balance after it. The total feeds the funded share on the dashboard.
Emergency log: urgent calls, response time and cost
One row for each emergency (burst pipe, no heat, sewer backup) with the hours to respond and the cost; a response check fills in.
Repair or replace: the decision for each aging item
One row for each item that keeps breaking with the repair cost, the replacement cost and the life left; the repair cost over the life left and the decision fill in.
Repair cost over the life left
Repair costs by kind: orders and spend
The eight kinds of repair with the number of work orders and the total spend, filled in from Work orders.
Tenant-caused repairs: cost, deposit and what was recovered
One row for each repair a tenant caused with the cost and the amount recovered; the tenant, the deposit held, the cost still to recover and the tenant phone fill in.
Safety checks: smoke alarms, handrails, panels and more
One row for each safety check with its due date and the date it was done; overdue or done on time and the days over fill in. Check your own local rules for what must be checked and how often.
